sections.h2: Robertson County offices that value and bill property
sections.html:
In Springfield, two elected offices divide the job. One, the Assessor of Property, decides what land and buildings are worth. The other, the County Trustee, sends out the bills and collects payment. The Register of Deeds files the deeds that tie the two together.

  • Assessor of Property: 521 S. Brown St., Springfield, 615-384-4311, weekday hours 8 to 4:30.
  • County Trustee: Room 161 of the Robertson County Office Building, 515 S. Brown St., 615-384-4238, Monday through Friday until 4:30 p.m.
  • Register of Deeds: same weekday schedule.

With so many parcels passing through the Trustee's hands, get any payoff figure in writing and do not rely on a phone estimate.

sections.h2: Robertson County housing and what it means for a sale
sections.html: Robertson County sits on the Kentucky line and belongs to the Nashville metropolitan area. Mid 2025 estimates count 80,175 residents, which is 10.1 percent above the 2020 base of 72,809. The typical owned home is valued at $335,000 for 2020 to 2024, household income runs $83,047, and owners occupy 77.6 percent of homes. Median rent is $1,199 a month. Springfield is the county seat, and the county also includes Adams, Cedar Hill, Cross Plains, Greenbrier, Orlinda, Coopertown, Ridgetop and White House.

sections.h2: Tax calendar and late payment costs
sections.html:
You can pay from the first Monday of October through the last day of February. On March 1, and again at the start of each later month, state law piles on 1.5 percent interest.

Robertson County real property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Owner on this date carries tax liability for the tax year
First Monday of OctoberTaxes become payable; notices go out in early October once the commission has set the rate
Last day of FebruaryFinal day to pay without interest
March 11.5% interest begins, T.C.A. 67-5-2010
March 15Last day to pay a year-delinquent bill at the trustee's office
March 16 to 31Delinquent real property goes to the tax attorney, then a Chancery Court suit, T.C.A. 67-5-2404

If February 28 lands on a weekend, ask the trustee which day is the last for paying in the office.

sections.h2: Where can I send a Robertson County tax payment?
sections.html:
Several routes work, including the counter, mail, web, phone and bank draft. The trustee takes partial payments and prepayments for as long as a bill stays in that office.

  • In person: Room 161 of the county office building during office hours, or the drop box by the sliding front door.
  • Drive thru: a kiosk lane at the office building.
  • Local banks: The Farmers Bank (all branches) and United Community Bank in Springfield, current year only and October through February, with the paper notice in hand.
  • Online or phone: tnproptax.com or 1-877-556-4079. The vendor charges 2.50 percent on cards or $1.25 on e-checks, plus $0.30 for phone payments, and the county keeps none of it.
  • Mail: the postmark date counts for interest.
  • Auto draft: monthly on the 10th, with the enrollment form received before the first of the prior month.

Most mortgage servicers send payment in December. Confirm it posted at tnproptax.com long before March 1.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax if a house sells mid-year?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner carries the liability, although a sales contract can move the cost to someone else. The trustee has no record of those contracts, so making sure the bill is paid remains your responsibility.

Timing adds a wrinkle. The Assessor receives a copy of every recorded deed the next day, but about 90 days go by before the parcel shows the buyer's name. The notice follows whatever name was on file January 1, so the closing papers should settle who pays. Mortgage companies do not receive tax notices by mail.

Before closing, ask the trustee for a current balance on every parcel you own. Deeds are indexed under different spellings of a name, so a search by name alone can miss one.

sections.h2: How to dispute a Robertson County assessment
sections.html:
A dispute climbs three rungs: the Assessor's office, the local equalization board, then the state board. County boards typically open June 1 and sit until their caseload is cleared.

If the county board's answer disappoints you, you have until August 1 of that tax year, or 45 days after the notice date if that is later, to file at the state level (T.C.A. 67-5-1412(e)). Processing cost is capped at $10 per filing. Values are fixed as of January 1, so events after that date generally do not affect the value, and recent comparable sales are the strongest evidence of what a house is worth.

Search by owner name, address or parcel number on the state-run Tennessee Property Data site, which the Assessor links to, and compare the record with the real house before you pick up the phone.

sections.h2: Relief and special programs from the Trustee
sections.html:
The Trustee runs three programs for eligible owners: a Tax Relief Program, a Tax Freeze Program and a Wheel Tax Rebate. Call 615-384-4238 for current requirements and application timing.

Farmland owners should also know about greenbelt. The Assessor mails greenbelt applications within 90 days of a processed deed. If land leaves agricultural, forest or open space use, rollback taxes apply: the difference between use value and market value for the preceding three years for farm and forest land, or five years for open space. They are not a penalty, and they become delinquent March 15 of the following year (T.C.A. 67-5-1008(d)). Anyone selling acreage should ask the Assessor whether a change of use is coming.

sections.h2: Selling a Robertson County house with tax still due
sections.html:
Yes. The balance simply becomes part of the sale. Buyers, lenders and title companies all want the exact figure, so ask the trustee to put it in writing.

Where the bill sits depends on its age. A real property bill under one year delinquent stays with the trustee, who accepts partial payments. After it is turned over, you pay through Robertson County Chancery Court at 615-384-5650, and added costs apply. Delinquent personal property tax for 2015 through 2024 can be paid through American Financial Credit Services at 888-317-2327 extension 3.

  1. Find out from the trustee what stage each year's bill has reached.
  2. Get the payoff in writing for your expected closing date.
  3. Have the settlement statement list the trustee payoff on its own line.

A cash purchase can proceed even with tax outstanding, though weigh the payoff against the price on the table.

faqs.q: What is the Robertson County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: The last day of February ends the interest-free period, and 1.5 percent interest starts March 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Robertson County?
faqs.a: Room 161 of the county office building, 515 S. Brown St. in Springfield, takes payments, as do the drop box, the drive thru, two named local banks, tnproptax.com and the mail.

faqs.q: How long does a deed take to show up with the Robertson County Assessor?
faqs.a: About 90 days. The Assessor gets a copy the day after recording, then moves the parcel into the new owner's name. The tax bill goes to the January 1 owner until the next year.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Robertson County assessment after the county board meets?
faqs.a: Yes. The State Board of Equalization takes appeals filed by August 1 or within 45 days of the county board's notice, whichever comes later. Begin with the Assessor at 615-384-4311.

faqs.q: Does Robertson County have a property tax relief program for seniors?
faqs.a: The Trustee runs a Tax Relief Program and a Tax Freeze Program. Call 615-384-4238 for eligibility rules and application timing, because the trustee sets the current requirements.
